result.title: Dynamic Memory-enhanced Pattern Relevance Prediction for Long-tailed Graph Classification
result.summary: Long-tailed graph classification (LTGC) is common in real-world graph datasets, where a few large head graphs provide rich structural information while many smaller tail graphs offer fewer structural cues, making it harder to learn discriminative representations for tail graphs. To address this size-based imbalance, we propose Dynamic Memory-enhanced Pattern Relevance Prediction (DMPRP), which transfers structural patterns from head graphs to tail graphs. Given a graph representation as a query, a dynamic expert memory module inspired by Knowledge-diverse Experts (KDEX) generates a residual vector that augments the original representation. We train the module using co-occurrence triplets sampled from head graphs at the node, rooted subgraph, and random-walk neighborhood levels. Experiments on five graph classification benchmarks show that DMPRP improves tail performance, and ablation studies show that both the expert module and random-walk supervision contribute to these gains. A controlled experiment on PTC further examines pattern transfer when smaller graphs are denser than larger ones. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DMPRP-73A5.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向长尾图分类，提出 DMPRP：以图表示为查询，用受 KDEX 启发的动态专家记忆模块生成残差向量来增强原表示，并用头部图在节点、根子图与随机游走邻域三个粒度采样的共现三元组训练该模块。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其「外部记忆＋专家路由生成残差来更新内部表示」以及多粒度共现监督，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态更新与多层级轨迹监督提供可核查的借鉴线索。
